extracted.intended_audience: general readers and stakeholders (industry, government, NGOs, researchers) interested in offshore oil platform decommissioning and environmental policy
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and considerations for choosing and evaluating disposal or dismantling options for decommissioning large offshore oil structures (e.g., on-shore dismantling vs deep-sea disposal). Covers environmental assessment, technical feasibility, safety, regulatory and public acceptance aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contaminant inventory estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Base decommissioning decisions on estimates of the quantities of various pollutants, including PCBs, crude oil, heavy metals, and scale, calculated from operating activities and residual metal in the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shell based its decommissioning decisions on such estimates; DNV later audited and provided alternate estimates (e.g., hydrocarbons: Shell est. 50,700 kg; DNV est. 75,000–100,000 kg). Ensure inventories are independently verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste classification and handling (scale as low-level radioactive waste)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and classify residues (e.g., scale) appropriately — scale is considered low-level radioactive waste and is routinely dealt with on-shore with PPE to prevent inhalation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan handling, decontamination and worker protection consistent with the waste type; include appropriate personal protective equipment and containment protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical feasibility and structural integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess technical feasibility of chosen disposal/dismantling method, including structural integrity concerns (e.g., whether facility can be re-floated or will disintegrate during handling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brent Spar's storage section had been stressed/damaged, raising doubts about re-floating horizontally. Evaluate engineering complexity and risks of structural failure in shallow water or towing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupational health and safety risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider workforce health and safety risks for each option; some options (on-shore dismantling) may be more complex and hazardous to workers than alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shell cited lower workforce risk for deep-sea disposal; on-shore dismantling estimated to present greater hazard to workforce and require special procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost estimation and cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate and compare costs of disposal options (including indirect costs such as lost sales/reputational damage) and weigh against environmental benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: on-shore dismantling estimated at £41M; deep-sea disposal £17–20M; final operation cost to Shell reported between £60M and £100M when loss of sales were included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact and scenario modelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Model environmental impacts under multiple plausible scenarios (e.g., structure sinks intact releasing contaminants slowly; disintegrates releasing a single burst; catastrophic surface release) and assess impacts on seabed, marine life, seabirds and fisheries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep-sea disposal scenarios gave different down-current affected distances (e.g., 500 m vs 1,000 m) and durations; consider short- and long-term effects for each scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site selection constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply clear siting stipulations such as jurisdictional limits (e.g., within the UK exclusive economic zone) and adequate depth so a sunken structure poses no hazard to shipping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRS identified 12x12 mi squares for candidate sites (Maury Channel, North Feni Ridge, Rockall Trough) and required sufficient depth and remoteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive site surveys and sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out multi-method site investigations including seabed visualisation (ROV), sediment sampling (box core), particle size distribution, total organic carbon, contaminant analyses (heavy metals, PCBs, hydrocarbons, radionuclides), and benthic/faunal surveys (box core counts, beam trawl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRS undertook these methods to characterise topography, sediment chemistry, and infaunal communities; limited sampling extent can preclude detailed analysis for entire areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological community assessment (abundance/diversity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess infaunal and benthic communities for abundance and diversity to understand ecosystem sensitivity and baseline conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRS found high diversity and low abundance typical of unimpacted deep sediments; such data influence impact predictions and site comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precaution regarding deep-sea knowledge gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge limited understanding of deep-sea environments and apply precaution where effects cannot be reliably predicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greenpeace argued lack of understanding precluded reliable predictions; where uncertainty is high, apply conservative measures and precautionary principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data robustness and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure supporting documents and impact assessments are based on robust data, avoid unsubstantiated assumptions and conjecture, and cite named studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greenpeace criticised Shell's licence documents as 'highly conjectural' with minimal data. Independent audits (e.g., DNV) and transparent publication of methods/assumptions improve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent verification and auditing
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission independent reviews/audits of inventories, sampling and impact assessments to verify claims and maintain credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After controversy, Shell commissioned Det Norske Veritas (DNV) to audit contents; DNV endorsed many of Shell's initial estimates and corrected Greenpeace's overestimate of oil content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating a damaging precedent; consider cumulative impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether an accepted disposal method would set a precedent for future dumping and whether cumulative effects of similar disposals are acceptable under international agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greenpeace argued sea disposal would create a precedent undermining OSPAR conventions; signatory nations later agreed on onshore disposal of oil facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory compliance and permitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain required government approvals and ensure compliance with applicable national and international laws and conventions (e.g., licences, OSPAR obligations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UK government approved Shell's sinking plan in December 1994; later policy changed toward onshore disposal under OSPAR member agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult conservation bodies, fishing interests, regional authorities and other stakeholders as part of planning and licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shell began formal consultations with conservation bodies and fishing interests; stakeholder responses (e.g., German government objection) influenced outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public perception and reputational risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider public opinion, potential for consumer boycotts, political backlash and reputational damage when selecting disposal options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greenpeace's media campaign and consequent boycotts in northern Europe led Shell to withdraw plans; Shell cited intense public criticism and political hostility as reasons to abandon sea disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of reuse and material recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider options to reuse structural components or recycle materials (e.g., cutting hull into rings for quay extension) as alternatives to disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shell received suggestions for reuse; Stavanger Port Authority used Spar hull rings for a quay extension at Mekjarvik, saving material and energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecological role of structures as habitat
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the structure provides habitat value (e.g., cold-water coral colonies) and weigh ecological consequences of removal versus leaving parts in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lophelia pertusa colonies were found on Brent Spar legs; later studies show many North Sea rigs host such colonies, raising debate about leaving lower parts in situ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate sampling methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use correct sampling protocols to avoid erroneous estimates of contaminant quantities or other key parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greenpeace's incorrect sample collection led to a large overestimate of oil content; correct sampling and chain-of-custody are essential to credible claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency and emergency scenario planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for possible catastrophic outcomes (e.g., surface release) and associated emergency response measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep-sea disposal planners envisaged catastrophic failure scenarios that would affect sea birds and fisheries; include mitigation/response planning for such scenarios.
